main_point.en: Faith is believing Jesus’s words before seeing His works.

christ_connection.en: Jesus responded to those who came to Him in faith for physical healing. In a greater way, all who come to Jesus in faith for salvation from sin are forgiven and restored with God.

content.en:
46 So he came again to Cana in Galilee, where he had made the water wine. And at Capernaum there was an official whose son was ill. 
47 When this man heard that Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee, he went to him and asked him to come down and heal his son, for he was at the point of death. 
48 So Jesus said to him, “Unless you see signs and wonders you will not believe.”
Leaders: Spend time reflecting on how Jesus’s works have strengthened your belief. Our faith is steady and sure, rooted in hope and in proof of what we haven’t yet seen (Heb. 11:1).

“This official could be either a Jew or a Gentile, and if he was a Gentile, then the divine grace revealed in this story is even more remarkable. But John does not indicate that the official isa Gentile, so we cannot be certain. In any case, for many Jews a servant at Herod’s court would be little better than a Gentile, so the scandalous nature of God’s grace is evident here even if the official is a Jew.”¹

“The word ‘go’ is imperative, so the man has been commanded by the Savior of the world with a promise of life for his son. But if he left, according to his way of thinking, he would leave behind his one chance for help. Jesus demanded that his faith be desperate enough to trust his word, not just his visible works. Wonders may produce awe, but words produce faith.”²

“The man obeyed the word of Jesus without seeing the sign. In the ancient world miracles and acts of power were linked to the presence of the miracle worker, but here the healer refused to be present. The story therefore is an important illustration of the purpose for which John wrote the Gospel. Here believing the word is linked with not immediately seeing the sign.”³

According to the Gospel of John, Jesus performed two significant miracles in the town of Cana. The first miracle took place at the wedding where Jesus turned water into wine (John 2:1-11). After Jesus traveled through Judea and Samaria, He returned to Cana, where He performed a second miracle—the healing of the royal official’s son. Many biblical scholars believe this royal official was one of Herod’s officers who had heard of Jesus’s first miracle in Cana and then desperately pursued Jesus to help his sick son.⁴ The fact that the official asked Jesus to “come down” (4:47) and heal his son is consistent with the geography of the region: Cana is at a higher elevation in the hills, where Capernaum is down on the shore of the Sea of Galilee. Coming from Capernaum, the official would have traveled between 18 to 22 miles to reach Jesus in Cana. Verses 51-52 indicate that the official likely walked this long distance to Cana and back, given that he returned to his servants the day after he encountered Jesus.⁵ The official would have had many hours to think as he walked the dusty roads, desperately hoping that Jesus really would heal his son.

Justification refers to the moment when a person is declared righteous before God based on the righteousness of Jesus’s atoning death (Rom. 8:33-34). This act of declaration takes place through faith in Jesus and not as a result of human works or effort (Eph. 2:8-9). Through justification, a person is made to be in right standing before God, changing what was once a strained and hostile relationship to one of adoption into the family of God.

LORD, YOU ARE OUR GREAT AND POWERFUL HEALER. MAY WE HAVE CONFIDENT FAITH IN YOU, EVEN WHEN OUR PERSPECTIVES ARE LIMITED. GIVE US THE STRENGTH AND COURAGE TO WALK BY FAITH AND NOT BY SIGHT. PLEASE CONTINUE TO GROW OUR STUDENTS’ FAITH AS THEY PURSUE YOU.

Did you know that the longest road in the world is nearly 19,000 miles long? The Pan-American Highway is made up of a series of roads that starts in Prudhoe Bay, Alaska, and stretches south to the tip of Argentina, the lower reaches of South America.⁶

instructions.en:
These optional activities are designed to help your students interact. You'll find a Discussion Activity and a Cultural Connection, which touches on a relevant topic in today’s teen culture. Each group is different, so adapt these activities to fit your group’s needs. The goal is for students to connect more to the lesson as they connect to the topic and to one another.

SUPPLIES LIST: NONE

Ask the following questions, allowing time for students to share responses:

question.en: Who is the most powerful person you know?
Discuss a time you really needed someone’s help.
When have you hoped for something without knowing if it would happen?

content.en: When Jesus began His public ministry and demonstrated His ability to perform miracles, people responded in a variety of ways. Some people suspected and doubted Him, while others believed in Him. We can trust in Jesus’s ability to work powerfully in our lives. He is our Redeemer, who has the power and desire to save all who come to Him in faith.

cultural_connection.en: Have you ever wrestled with why God heals some people and not others? Christians aren’t immune to the effects of living in a fallen, broken world. Jesus often healed people’s sicknesses and diseases, and Scripture encourages us to pray for healing when we are sick (James 5:14, 16). Sometimes God heals, but sometimes He chooses not to heal on this side of eternity. If you’ve walked through a situation where God didn’t answer a prayer for healing, you aren’t alone in feeling disappointed, hurt, or confused. We don’t have to hide our hurt or disappointment from God. Instead, we go to Him; we hold on to the truth that He is our good, loving Father, who uses everything—even what’s painful—to draw us close and make us more like Jesus (Rom. 8:28). We can invite Jesus into our suffering, knowing He sympathizes with our weaknesses and struggles because He also suffered here (Heb. 4:15). God always heals those who seek Him for spiritual healing. All who confess Jesus as Lord are saved (Rom. 10:9), and we have hope that no matter what happens on earth, we will spend eternity in heaven with no more pain, sickness, or disease.

question.en: What is the difference between needing something and being desperate for something? When have you felt desperate?

answer.en: Leaders: Share context about the distance from Capernaum to Cana. Desperation implies having an extreme and urgent need and may lead to risky or reckless behavior in an attempt to find answers. Maybe you’ve felt desperate for relief from pain or for a loved one’s healing. The royal official was clearly desperate to find healing for his sick son and traveled a long distance to seek Jesus’s help. Situations like these often lead us to Jesus when we realize we have nowhere else to turn. But the truth is that we can go to Jesus with every need because He cares about them all—both big and small.

question.en: How are we all in the same desperate situation before God? Why can’t we fix it?

answer.en: We all have the same fundamental problem as human beings: We are spiritually dead because our sin separates us from God (Rom. 3:23; 6:23). We can’t earn salvation or forgiveness with our good works or by following God’s law. Because God is good, holy, and just, He can’t overlook sin or sweep it under the rug. This leaves us in a desperate situation because we are all guilty before God and deserving of death (John 3:18). Thankfully, God provided a way for us to be fully justified before Him through Jesus’s sacrificial death on our behalf. Jesus met us in our desperation and fixed what we couldn’t fix on our own.

question.en: When we’re desperate, why do we often run to other things or people instead of Jesus? How does everything else fail us?

answer.en: Sometimes our earthly needs feel like the most significant issues we face. For example: We may feel desperate for belonging. And instead of seeking godly friends to walk with us, we settle for toxic friendships that distract us from following Jesus. To avoid loneliness, we settle for belonging in the wrong places. In our desperation, we often turn to other people or the things of this world instead of looking to God to rescue us or help us. However, no temporary solution can truly save us. No matter how great our earthly needs are, our spiritual need is greater. Jesus proved that He cares about our needs by coming to our broken world to save us from our sin. If we can trust Jesus with our greatest need—forgiveness of our sin—then we can trust Him to meet our other needs as well. Trusting Him with our eternal life means that we can also trust Him with our earthly life.

question.en: How would you define genuine belief in Jesus?

answer.en: Genuine belief in Jesus involves both our head and our heart—our mind and our will. We must believe that He is the Son of God, sent to the world to save us from our sin. But only mentally acknowledging that Jesus is real is not enough to save us. The demons believe Jesus is real but do not follow Him (James 2:19). We must confess that Jesus is Lord and believe in our hearts that God raised Him from the dead (Rom. 10:9). Saving belief means that we believe in Jesus and obey what He says. Faith requires action. If we love Jesus, we must keep His commands (John 14:15). Just like the royal official believed and acted on what Jesus told him, we must do the same. True followers of Jesus must follow His commands to turn from our sinful ways and honor Him with our lives.

question.en: Why do you think we sometimes struggle to take Jesus at His word or to trust His promises?

answer.en: Trusting people can be difficult if they’ve let you down or disappointed you. We more easily trust people when we see their good character. Thankfully, Jesus is perfectly trustworthy. Jesus wants us to take Him at His word, and He is kind enough to show us that we have good reasons to trust Him. Jesus backs up His words with action. He proved His power and authority by performing signs and miracles, like healing the royal official’s son. Jesus proved that He loves us by dying on the cross for our sins. He demonstrated His power as the Messiah through His death and resurrection, which He predicted beforehand. Jesus knows that our limited human perspective can make it difficult for us to trust Him, so we can look to His power and fulfilled promises to strengthen our faith.

question.en: What does Jesus’s ability and willingness to heal people like the royal official’s son reveal about Him?

answer.en: Some scholars believe that the royal official wasn’t Jewish but a Roman Gentile. Jesus’s ability to heal shows that He is the Messiah, and His willingness to heal a Gentile shows that He loves and cares for all people. Not only did Jesus’s healings fulfill Old Testament prophecies about what the Messiah would do (Matt. 8:17), but they also showed us His heart. Jesus had compassion for those who were sick or struggling with sin and those who wanted to be near to Him. Jesus is gentle and lowly at heart (Matt. 11:29) and offers grace and mercy to those who come to Him. He is our kind and loving Savior, who laid down His life for us so that we could have fellowship with Him forever.

question.en: In what situation is Jesus asking you to trust Him before seeing the results? What would it look like to have faith before seeing the outcome?

answer.en: When Jesus told the royal official that his son would live, the man believed Jesus would be true to His word. He made the long journey to Capernaum, trusting Jesus had healed his son before seeing the proof. We are called to have this same confidence in Jesus’s words, but this can be challenging when we are in a season of waiting. Maybe you are waiting to find a solid group of friends. Maybe you’re waiting for a college admissions letter or a scholarship opportunity. Maybe you’re waiting to hear back from a doctor about test results. In the “in between” times, we are called to walk by faith and not by sight (2 Cor. 5:7)—to believe before we see. Knowing that we serve a powerful and merciful Savior is comforting. Jesus has already met our greatest need by providing the way for us to be restored to God. He promises to be with us and give us the strength we need to follow Him every day (Phil. 4:13). Remembering Jesus’s power and His love for us will help us trust Him while we wait to see the outcome.

content.en: Can you imagine how the Israelites felt as they came up on the body of water? The situation must’ve felt desperate: the Egyptians behind them, the water in front of them, and nowhere to go. Can you picture walking on dry land through the walls of the sea, knowing that just a few minutes earlier, there was no way out? They had been slaves in Egypt for 400 years before God sent Moses to rescue them, so we can understand any confusion they had when God powerfully parted the waters. Not long after this miraculous moment, the people started complaining about hunger, accusing God of leading them into the wilderness to die. As outsiders looking in, we get frustrated with the Israelites and are shocked that they want to go back to Egypt—to slavery. But imagine if they were reading a story about your life and how God has worked to rescue you; would they also get frustrated over how quickly you forget and turn to worldly comforts to satisfy your desires or to fit in? Why do we so easily forget? Our world, bodies, and minds are broken. Sin easily distracts us with a promise of temporary pleasure, but God is more wonderful than those fleeting moments. By sending Jesus to take the punishment for your sins, He has done more for you than anything the world can offer you. When you call on the Lord for salvation, you become the dwelling place for the Holy Spirit, who works to transform your heart and mind. The next time you find yourself in a desperate situation, remember that the same power that parted the Red Sea is the same power living inside of you.

question.en: When you face a challenging situation, what is the first thing you turn to as a way of escape? Why?
Recall a Red Sea moment—when you thought that a good outcome was impossible. How did God make a way and work it out?

prayer.en: God, thank You for all the ways You have rescued me. If all You ever did was save me from my sins, that would be enough. Help me to always remember the signs and wonders You have used to rescue me.

content.en: Most of us don’t immediately trust people we’ve just met. Trusting new people is much easier when another trusted friend has already tested and approved of their character and integrity. In a way, the Bible does this for us. Scripture is full of people who lived lives just like us—who faced moments requiring great faith in God to have their back. Because of these testimonies in Scripture, when you surrender your life to Christ through faith, you aren’t acting in blind faith. God has proven over and over again that He takes care of His people. Hebrews 11 is known as the “Hall of Faith” because the people listed there faced circumstances beyond their control. Many times, they didn’t know what was going to happen, but they took the next step in faith because they trusted the One guiding their steps. They had unwavering faith in God because they witnessed His unwavering commitment to work all things for their good and His glory (Rom. 8:28). God is for us; He is committed to us. We can move confidently through the unknown because we know God’s character through the stories in His Word. You can’t see God with your eyes, but your relationship with Him is as real as it gets, as real as your relationship with your closest friend. If you are waiting for a clear sign from God to know if you can trust Him, you can look in His Word. You can confidently move in faith because God has already proven He is faithful to take care of you.

question.en: Is it easy for you to have faith in God even though you cannot see Him? Why or why not?
When have you faced a situation that was beyond your control? In what ways did God take care of you?

prayer.en: Thank You for Your unwavering faithfulness to love and take care of me. I trust that You are working all things for my good, even when I can’t see it. Help me to walk confidently into the unknown because You are there.

content.en: Have you ever been to a football game in your hometown? An interesting thing happens as the athletes on the field grow up and sit in the stands as adults. People often still see them as who they were when they were students. Today’s reading is the perfect example of this phenomenon. Jesus met with a Samaritan woman and was flooded with other Samaritans, who were eager to meet Him. The Jews were God’s chosen people from which Jesus descended, and they despised the Samaritans. But Jesus gave them His time and attention anyway. As Jesus left for Galilee, He said that aman does not have honor in his hometown. If Jesus was to sit in the football stands in Galilee, the people would struggle to see Him as anyone other than the boy they watched grow up there. They didn’t give Jesus the honor He deserved. When He arrived in Galilee, some accepted Him only because they had seen His works in Jerusalem. The Samaritans believed without seeing, but the Jews needed to see before they believed. Jesus’s mission was to save both the Jews and the Gentiles. Anyone lost in sin can call on the name of the Lord and be saved. Though the Jews ultimately rejected Jesus, He became a sacrifice for their sins. His sacrifice was for every person and group, including you.

question.en: Do you only trust God when you have seen Him work? What about when He feels silent?
What sins are you hiding because you fear God can’t or won’t forgive you? Confess them to God today.

prayer.en: Thank You, God, for Jesus’s sacrifice for my sins. Thank You for choosing all people to bless with Your mercy and grace. Help me show this love to everyone today.

content.en: What is your definition of the word “anything”? As it is used in this Scripture, it encompasses everything; nothing is left out. Think back to this week’s lesson. The father was desperate for his son’s healing. When Jesus told him that his son was healed, the man believed, even though he hadn’t seen his son yet. When you read, “Do not be anxious about anything,” your mind may go to a situation that is the exception. You may feel like your situation is beyond help, even from God. You may believe that God can work things out for other people, but your case is different, too difficult. What Scripture says is true: No situation in your life is too far out of God’s reach for Him to take care of. Everything means everything. The Scripture goes on to say that you only need to turn over everything to God through prayer. He cares. He wants to meet you where you are. He wants to take the burden you are carrying and replace your anxiety with peace. When you let go of control and give it over to God, the peace that surpasses all understanding will cover your mind and dissolve the worry. Because of Jesus and with the help of the Holy Spirit, we have access to peace. You can’t do anything to earn it; instead, the God of all creation sees you, cares about you, and takes care of you. He sent Jesus to create a way for you to experience His peace. You must simply believe.

question.en: Recall a time when you felt desperate for God’s peace in a situation. Did you give it over to Him through prayer? How did He provide peace?
Do you believe that God cares for you and wants to take care of you in every situation? Why or why not?

prayer.en: God, You are so good and kind. Thank You for showing me compassion, and by Your authority, forgiving my sins.

content.en: What is the most painful situation or season you have ever been in? Was finding meaning in it easy or difficult? Your hardest, most desperate situations can be used for good and for God’s glory. Saying we believe this is easy, but actually believing it is more difficult when you’re in the middle of desperate times. Those times test whether or not we believe what we claim. In today’s passage, the father learns that his son was healed in the same moment Jesus said he was healed. This moment could have easily been overlooked or missed. In today’s culture, we tend to believe that miracles like this don’t happen. How often do we miss the opportunity to point others to Jesus because we do not see Jesus’s work happening right in front of us? This father didn’t miss it; he knew Jesus had healed his son. The most painful moment of his life was redeemed by Jesus, and he told everyone about it. We can use this story as a model for us to imitate: The father invited Jesus into a very desperate situation because he knew Jesus was the only One who could fix it. Then, he invited everyone else into the story so that they could see that Jesus could help them too. What about you? What painful situation are you in right now, and how have you looked to Jesus to redeem it? Friend, Jesus redeeming the hardest seasons of your life is just as possible for you as it was for this young boy and his father. The next step for you is simple: Invite Jesus to fix it, and then tell anyone who will listen about His goodness.

question.en: Do you struggle to allow God to use your difficult seasons for your good and His glory? Explain.
Recall a time when you or someone you know went through a painful time but were able to use it to spread the gospel. What does this show you about our pain?

prayer.en: Thank You, God, for working all things for my good and Your glory. You are the only One who can redeem my pain. Please give me the courage to use difficult situations in my life to spread the message of Your goodness and grace.
